name: unote
author: Sam Poplett
// type: ESM, so Vercel compiles api/index.ts as an ES module. Without this it defaults to CommonJS and require()ing the ESM server throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM at runtime, a failure that only appears once deployed.
// main: Entry for the Electron shell only. electron-builder reads it to find the packaged main process; nothing imports this package.
description: Unote: a student notebook. Notion x Obsidian x Google Docs, local-first, AI-powered.

scripts.dev: concurrently -n api,web -c blue,magenta "npm run dev -w server" "npm run dev -w web"
scripts.test: npm run test -w server && npm run test -w web

// dependencies: electron-updater is imported by the packaged main process AT RUNTIME, so it has to be a production dependency: electron-builder bundles `dependencies` into the asar and leaves `devDependencies` out entirely. As a devDependency it built green, published green, installed fine, and then died on first launch with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND - the only place that failure can appear is a real install, which is why v0.1.0 shipped broken. Note the contrast with `electron` below: that one is correctly a devDependency, because the packaged app IS the Electron runtime and never resolves it from node_modules.
